sections.text: I am the Heat of the Sun, I release and hold back the Rains. I am Death and Immortality; I am Being and Not-Being.

Those who are versed in the scriptures, who drink the mystic Soma-juice and are purified from sin, but who while worshipping Me with sacrifices pray that I will lead them to heaven; they reach the holy world where lives the Controller of the Powers of Nature, and they enjoy the feasts of Paradise.

Yet although they enjoy the spacious glories of Paradise, nevertheless, when their merit is exhausted, they are born again into this world of mortals. They have followed the letter of the scriptures, yet because they have sought but to fulfill their own desires, they must depart and return again and again.

In the beginning of Bhagavad Gita, the first six chapters, we have learned about ourselves as the Great Mahavakya from Upanishad Tattvamasi. That thou art that which you are seeking, that which is in control of this universe and my life. Who is that that Im seeking is that you are that. So that paradigm shift about the one Im seeking is not away from me, but my own self. And then we obviously have seen that the one which I consider myself me is just an equipment which I use to transact with this world. What I consider myself with this body, this mind, this intellect.
In chapter two we have this paradigm shift that thats not you. Thats actually a vehicle you use to transact with this world. But you are imperishable, immutable, unborn, never dying. Thats a paradigm shift we have learned in the in the second chapter then we also learned about the karma yoga act. I must as an individual in this world. So I do not perpetuate this ignorance I have about myself.
So we all learned about karma yoga. Selfless actions will purify my mind and intellect, the internal instrument so that Ill be able to see the reality as is where myself then the universal self has no duality. It is something similar to my room space. Right now I see is completely separated from the outside. But from another developer who wants to build a big building, this space is part of the space outside. And then obviously we have seen how to get the Karma Sanyas renunciation in actions by knowledge.
By knowing that I am not the doer, I can renounce my actions. I right now take the doership and ownership of my actions. Except I am not really ready to face the consequences. And when the consequences come, I blame other people. World was unfair, society is unjust. People dont recognize my contribution.
All of that is simply because of my lack of understanding that I am not the doer. I have very little capacity to act on my own. Im just a part of this whole fabric which is called this universe. And Im just this minute part which only can function when other parts function in its own way. So theres a Gnana Karma Sanyas Yoga. Once the knowledge takes place that I am not by individual and island who is capable of acting that I give up my ownership of my actions and I start accepting my role as a part in this whole. And then we obviously see in meditation, Dhyana Yoga how to now reflect and contemplate on myself so I can wipe this ignorance out of myself.
Those are the first six chapters we learned about ourselves. We are not with who think we are. Bhagavan said, you are part of my own self. The next three chapters, 7, 8, and 9, are about That -- we learned about Tat first. Tat means That -- we learned about That. Then we said, who is That which Im seeking as the Lord of this universe?
Therefore Lord of my own self. Bhagavan gave his identity in the last three chapters saying I am who pervades in this entire universe in my unmanifest form, I am the source of this universe. Ill be the resting place for this universe. Everything comes out of me, everything dissolves in me. But we can recognize that. So this chapter Chapter 9 says Raja Vidya Raja Guya Yoga opened with a profound statement by Bhagavan said I manifest in this entire Jagat in my unmanifest form.
But people fail to recognize it out of their own ignorance. The world is full of Mudhas. They fail to recognize because of their own different identifications, notions, desires -- Mogha Asha, Mogha Karmaha. Bhagavan said you need the right equipment to recognize something which is unmanifest. There are radio waves in this room. Im not sure now that theyve all gone digital.
But think about how analog radio waves work. Radio waves are wireless. What are the waves which make my wireless phone work? To make them manifest, I need equipment. And when that equipment is fine-tuned and pointed in the right direction, it will manifest. Yesterday I was listening to one of these Gujarati Kathas by Ramesh bhai Oza.
And I said this Samsar. We are completely surrounded by this Samsar that is constantly changing by this Maya. We are trying to find its end. Where does this Maya end? They say all over vernacular language said Sansar. You have to cross this Sansar, this ocean of Sansar.
And for that you need a boat. He said that boat, Ramesh bhai, is your body, this mind, and this intellect. Its not an ordinary boat -- its like a luxury liner. It is fully equipped with all that you need to cross over this ocean in a very luxurious way. But we fail to recognize the goal of this boat and direct it towards other things.
So we go in circles. Our scripture says that the ultimate goal of human life is to recognize your own self, your own reality, who you really are. In this evolution from a single-cell amoeba to where we are now, we are fully equipped to realize who we are. But we fail to recognize that. Why? Traividya mam somapaha puta papa yajnaih ishtva svargantim prarthayante.
Te punya masadya surendra lokam asnanti divyan divi deva bhogan. How does this work? It works as simply as this: wherever you put your effort, whatever your goal is, that is what you will achieve. What do I want to become? We ask our little children all the time, What do you want to become when you grow up? Well, I want to be a fireman.
We never let him try to become a fireman. The parents say, Oh no, okay, thats a great idea. But no, no, youre not becoming a fireman. We are not going to let you do that. The point is: we dont always put our efforts into what we truly want to achieve. We achieve whatever we actually put our efforts into.
Now here were not talking about people who are completely deluded and dont know what they are doing. Here are the people who we consider ourselves to be like -- people who say, Look, I really dont need to do anything more. Im a good man doing good things. So what else do I need to do? And I constantly say doing good is not good enough.
The knowledge about yourself and what youre trying to achieve is very important before you start any action. So here it says traividya. Those who are expert in three Vedas, those who have learned three Vedas -- they are knowledgeable people. They have jnana in the Vedas. They are somapaha -- puta papa.
Somapaha means one who has drunk that soma drink. The soma drink was offered into the Agni, and then as prasad, you take it in a small quantity at the end of the Yajna. It indicates that the ritual is over and Im taking whatever came out of this Yajna. Just like when you go to the temple, at the end of the Aarti, Panditji is standing there distributing the Charnamrit. It basically indicates that the performing of the Puja is over. Thats the conclusion of my actions.
And Im taking whatever will come out of the action. They are also purified of the sins. They dont have any evil qualities. They are not evil doers. They are the Veda knowers. They have done the rituals as indicated in the Vedas.
They are free from sins. Yajnaih Ishtva Svargantim Prarthayante. Having performed this sacrifice of the Yajna, what does their desire say? They want to achieve heaven. Anything good we do -- what is the ultimate goal? I am doing this Puja, I am doing these actions.
In the end what we want is heaven. I can have all the good things in life and no sorrows. So Swarganti Parthayanti, the Purnya Masadya, Surendra Loka, Asnanti Divyan Divideva Bhagaana. So having earned all this merits of the good deeds they are doing the knowledge they have gathered from the Vedas. Vedas means the books of knowledge. So our Vedas are now expanded to many, many, many sciences.
Knowing all this, I perform actions in a field of my chosen field and ask for Swarga. O Lord, give me a situation where there is no sorrow ever, always there is happiness. So they achieve the Surendra Loka. The Loka of the Devas. The place of Devalok. And we have talked about there are various Lokas.
You know, from Go Loka to Brahma Loka. After all they are all in my mind. When I am in a complete control and happiness, I feel I am in heaven. Things are going right. Kids are doing fine job. Nobody is bothering me.
People are respecting me. Everybody is saying Rajan, you are doing wonderful. Meena is not complaining. Surendra Loka Hatha Bhagawan says you reach that Surendra Loka. People achieve that state of Surendra Loka, Asnanti Divya Divideva Bhogan. Theyre enjoying all these divine pleasures which we learn in this Purana all the time.
These Apsaras are dancing. You know, somebody is doing this. Beautiful gardens, no drought anywhere. You enjoy all the Bhogas. But then I say tetam bhuktva swargalokam vishalam Enjoying these vast heavens and vast enjoyments in the heavens. Chine punya martha lo KE vishante.
But once those punyas are exhausted -- no matter how infinite you think they are -- consider Bill Gates, the wealthiest person in this world. You can still count his wealth, cant you? We can put a number to it. An expert CPA sits down, looks at his books, and comes up with this is your wealth. It can be spent. It may take longer than my wealth, maybe a very long time, but it can be exhausted, and it will be exhausted at some point. Bill Gates descendants, whoever they may be, will eventually not have anything.
I remember one Gujarati poem I heard is Sagaadi tami sa alamna bhik magda shariya sah alam who was the Mughal emperor. He said, Ive seen his descendants begging in the street. Saga di tam es salam na bhik makta serhiye. So any wealth, no matter how infinite seem right now, will be exhausted in time. The same applies to you. Any amount of good deeds and good merits you have done to achieve these heavenly pleasures -- you will get them according to your efforts, according to your ability.
But once you reach there and enjoy those vast heavens, at some point they will exhaust, and youre back to square one. Youre going to start from where you left off. Just like going on a vacation -- at the end of the vacation, you are back to square one, working for another 50 weeks to earn two weeks of vacation again. Evam Trayi Dharmam Anuprapanna Gatagatam Kama Kama Labhante. Thus, as described in the Vedas, they attain the state of going and coming.
I perform good actions, achieve heavens, come back, keep performing good actions, go back and coming back. Obviously we say well thats good enough for me. And Bhagawan says thats why we are stuck into it, no? Because we are so addicted to this heavens, addicted to the results of my good actions that we continue to go back and forth, go back and forth into it.

Krishna describes people who are learned in the Vedas (traividya), who perform rituals correctly (yajnair ishtva), who are purified of sins (puta-papa) - yet they pray for heaven (svargati prarthayante). They achieve what they seek: divine pleasures in celestial realms. But here is the sobering truth - kshine punye martya lokam vishanti - when their merit is exhausted, they return to the mortal world. Even Bill Gates wealth, though seemingly infinite, can be counted and eventually spent. So too, any accumulation of punya (merit), no matter how vast, will eventually deplete.
This is the cosmic trap: gatagatam kama-kama labhante - those driven by desires attain going and coming, an endless cycle of earning, enjoying, depleting, and returning. Like working 50 weeks for a 2-week vacation, then returning to work again, we strive for temporary heavens only to start over. We have a luxury liner of body-mind-intellect fully equipped to cross the ocean of samsara, yet we sail in circles, never reaching the far shore.
Honest self-assessment: What is the goal of your spiritual practice? Is it a better rebirth, a more comfortable life, heavenly rewards? These are legitimate desires, but Krishna invites you to something greater - liberation from the cycle itself. This week, examine your deepest motivations. Are you seeking temporary relief or permanent freedom? The practices may look similar externally, but the intention determines the destination. What would shift if your goal became not better experiences within the dream, but awakening from the dream altogether?
